results.title: 7 AI Specialist Interview Questions and Answers - Himalayas
results.content: Describe a time you led development and deployment of an AI model in production with strict data privacy (GDPR) constraints. * Describe remediation actions: rollback recent model changes, retrain with new regional data, implement stratified models or region-specific calibration, and add long-term fixes like automated drift detection and retraining pipelines. * Deployment: set guardrails—monitoring for data drift, prediction distribution, calibration, and automated alerts; provide model cards and documentation for repeatability; include rollback and human-in-the-loop processes for high-risk predictions. Before deployment, I'd create a monitoring plan for data drift and calibration, add a human-in-the-loop triage for high-risk outputs, and produce documentation and model cards. * Describe concrete trade-offs you proposed (e.g., latency vs privacy, model accuracy vs explainability) and how you justified them with data or risk analysis. Product wanted aggressive personalization to increase AOV, data scientists pushed complex models requiring more user data, while security/legal raised privacy and compliance concerns.

results.title: Detection Engineering Lifecycle: An Integrated Approach to ...
results.content: This blog post defines and analyzes each phase of the detection engineering lifecycle — including Threat Intelligence, Vulnerability Management, Red Team/Penetration Testing, Security Engineering, Security Operations, Incident Response, Security Architecture, and Automation — and explains how they interrelate to form a continuous improvement loop. We then propose a governance framework for developing and deploying detections (“path to production”) using detection-as-code principles: version control, peer review, automated testing (unit, integration), pre-production breach-and-attack simulation (BAS) validation, CI/CD pipelines, and post-deployment KPIs. Strategies for drift monitoring are specified, covering configuration drift, data source health, and periodic rule re-certification to ensure detections remain effective over time. **In practice, mature security programs blend elements of all these approaches.** A CTI-driven approach grounded in real adversary TTPs provides a threat-informed baseline — focusing on likely attack methods — which is supported by asset criticality considerations (to ensure important assets are well monitored) and kill-chain coverage (to ensure balance and depth in detection).
